SOURCE: board DM msg 614 (human:forrest, 2026-09-09T21:53Z): 'We can auto start, your call' -- the yes to the offer in msg 613 to file dashboard supervision as its own item. Filed by the CTO on the board member's behalf.

WHAT: install the Lattice dashboard as a supervised launchd user agent on the host, on the exact pattern of the advance watcher (apps/chat/watch/com.american-software.advance-watcher.plist.template + the Install/Uninstall/Restart sections of apps/chat/watch/README.md). Deliverables are a plist template, a render/validate recipe, README sections, and a guard -- NOT the host install itself (decision 3).

WHY: AS-93 makes chat's AS-n deep links infer the dashboard host from the page (loopback -> :8799, tailnet -> :8443). That is useless from the phone unless something is listening. Today the ONLY thing serving :8799 is a hand-started process in a Claude Code live session: at filing time pid 37867 is '/Users/forrest/.local/bin/lattice dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8799', parented by a Claude Code zsh snapshot shell (pid 37865). When that session ends, every link dies -- on the phone and on the Mac. No launchd job exists for it; the advance watcher got one on AS-7, the dashboard never did. AS-10 deliberately kept the dashboard out of compose (vendor tooling that ships with the pipx-installed Lattice CLI, same category as git -- apps/chat/README.md 'Links to Lattice'); that decision stands. Host supervision is the consistent answer: the watcher is the precedent, not compose.

HOW IT IS SERVED TODAY (facts the plan must not re-derive):
  - Binary: /Users/forrest/.local/bin/lattice (pipx; python 3.14 from homebrew). Command in use: lattice dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8799. It is read-only and finds .lattice/ by walking up from its cwd, so WorkingDirectory MUST be the repo root (the main checkout, pinned to master).
  - Tailnet path: https://forrests-newer-macbook.tail3f3c29.ts.net:8443 -> 127.0.0.1:8799 via Tailscale serve (chat itself is served on 443 -> 8347 the same way). The serve mapping lives in tailscaled's state, not in this repo. ASSUMPTION to verify in planning ('tailscale serve status' -- a host action): it persists across reboot on its own. If it does not, that is a second, separate host record; note it, do not fold it in.
  - The dashboard supports graceful restart on SIGHUP ('lattice restart' from another terminal), so the supervised job can be bounced without bootout/bootstrap.

DECISIONS (CTO):
  1. Bind stays 127.0.0.1. The dashboard exposes the whole board; tailnet reach goes ONLY through Tailscale serve (Tailscale-authenticated). Never 0.0.0.0. This is a property with a falsifier (AC-2).
  2. The launchd job becomes the ONE owner of :8799. Hand-running 'lattice dashboard' beside it is what the README now tells you not to do; use 'lattice restart' to bounce it. Today's live-session process must be stopped before bootstrap or the job crash-loops on EADDRINUSE (AC-4).
  3. Installing is a host action (launchctl, ~/Library/LaunchAgents) that a headless tick cannot perform -- same as the watcher (apps/chat/watch/README.md 'After any change to this watcher: restart it'). The task ends in needs_human with the exact bootstrap commands; the board or a live session runs them and records the observation (AC-3). Do not force past this.
  4. Placement: this is chat tooling under apps/chat/watch/ (the tooling directory the board's msg 557 rule names), so it is IN the critical Chat set. Ordering within the set is recorded on AS-93 (comment) and in CLAUDE.md section 'Scheduling priority': AS-93 first, this task second, then the rest by age.
  5. Suggested file: apps/chat/watch/com.american-software.lattice-dashboard.plist.template with __REPO_ROOT__ / __LATTICE_BIN__ / __PATH__ placeholders, KeepAlive + RunAtLoad, stdout/stderr to apps/chat/data/logs/lattice-dashboard.out.log and .err.log. Planner may restructure; the label prefix com.american-software. and the logs directory are fixed.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (M4: each property names the input that must make the mechanism report a violation; satisfied only by an OBSERVED red, never by an argument):
  AC-1  The README's render recipe (sed over the template) produces a plist that 'plutil -lint' accepts. Falsifier: in a scratch copy, break the template XML and observe plutil red.
  AC-2  A guard (test or script, runnable by the reviewer) asserts the rendered ProgramArguments are exactly [<lattice bin>, dashboard, --host, 127.0.0.1, --port, 8799] and WorkingDirectory is the repo root. Falsifier: mutate a scratch copy to --host 0.0.0.0 and observe the guard red; restore; prove with git diff --exit-code.
  AC-3  Host verification, recorded on this task by whoever runs the bootstrap: 'launchctl print gui/<uid>/com.american-software.lattice-dashboard' shows state = running; GET http://127.0.0.1:8799/ returns 200; kill the dashboard pid; KeepAlive relaunches it and 8799 returns 200 again within 30 s. Quote all four observations.
  AC-4  Single owner of the port: with the job up, a manual 'lattice dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8799' fails to bind (observed, quoted) -- and the README says so, plus the pre-bootstrap step 'stop any live-session dashboard first' with the pgrep line that finds it.
  AC-5  Docs: apps/chat/watch/README.md gains Install/Uninstall/Restart sections for the dashboard mirroring the watcher's (including 'lattice restart' for SIGHUP), and apps/chat/README.md 'Links to Lattice' replaces 'run lattice dashboard to make them resolve' with the supervised service (keep the AS-10 not-in-compose rationale). Review compares the two README sections side by side.
  AC-6  If any suite numbers are quoted: docker compose run --rm --build test with the 'Image ... Built' line quoted (CLAUDE.md corollary). If nothing in the compose suite is touched, say so explicitly instead of quoting a number.

OUT OF SCOPE: containerizing the dashboard (AS-10 decision stands); making Tailscale serve config a repo artifact; the chat sidebar reporting dashboard liveness (a follow-up if the board wants the indicator).

RELATION: independent in build terms from AS-93 (either merges first without breaking the other); they are the two halves of one board-facing outcome -- links that work from the phone without a live session. Linked to AS-93 and AS-10 as related work, deliberately NOT depends_on in either direction so neither holds the other back in lattice next.

CTO — two bindings for this task's planner, arising from the board's comment on AS-93 ("keep in mind for this the lattice port is not fixed", dashboard:web 2026-09-10T15:30Z) and my ruling there. Both sit inside this task's EXISTING scope; neither widens it.

CONTEXT. I ruled that AS-93 merges as built with its two constants (LOOPBACK_PORT=8799, REMOTE_PORT=8443), and that THIS task is what makes the loopback port stop being ambient: your decision 2 already says the launchd job is the one owner of :8799, and your AC-2 already asserts the rendered ProgramArguments contain `--port 8799` with a mutation falsifier. That is the actual answer to the board's comment — after this task the port is declared by a committed artifact under a guard, rather than by whatever a live session happened to type. Full reasoning is the ruling comment on AS-93; read it before planning.

BINDING 1 — the plist declares 8799, not a fresh port. Verified this tick: 8799 is the Lattice CLI's own default (`@click.option("--port", default=8799)`, lattice/cli/dashboard_cmd.py:49; `lattice restart` defaults to the same at :143), and the live Tailscale serve mapping is `:8443 -> http://127.0.0.1:8799`. Choosing any other port in this task would silently break both AS-93 constants AND the serve mapping at once. If the planner believes a different port is right, that is a needs_human, not a plan decision.

BINDING 2 — the README must name all three legs (this is a specification of your AC-5, which already puts both READMEs in scope, not new scope). The port is a three-legged coupling and the next person to move it must find the whole list in one place:
  L1  the launchd plist's `--port` (this task's artifact)
  L2  the Tailscale serve mapping `:8443 -> 127.0.0.1:8799` — host state in tailscaled, NOT a repo artifact, and chat cannot observe it
  L3  `LOOPBACK_PORT` / `REMOTE_PORT` in apps/chat/public/dashboard-link.js (AS-93)
Say plainly that moving any one alone breaks a surface, and which: L1 alone kills the phone and the Mac; L1+L2 kills the Mac; L1+L3 without L2 kills the phone. Also say that `LATTICE_DASHBOARD_URL` does NOT rescue this — it is one verbatim base, so it can say "this URL everywhere" but never "port X on loopback, port Y over the tailnet"; pointing it at a non-8799 loopback URL fixes the Mac and re-breaks the phone. Keep it to a short block; it is a signpost, not an essay.

STILL OUT OF SCOPE, unchanged: making the Tailscale serve config a repo artifact. Naming L2 in prose is not importing it. If the planner finds during the serve-persistence check (your description's parked assumption) that the mapping does NOT survive reboot, that is a separate host record — note it and do not fold it in.

RELATED: AS-96 is filed and contingent on the board's answer — one declared port value shared across L1/L2/L3. It depends_on this task and AS-93. Do not pre-build for it here; the two bindings above are all this task owes the problem.

Planner breadcrumb (CTO). Plan written: four deliverables under apps/chat/ — the plist template (explicit --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8799, KeepAlive+RunAtLoad, logs under data/logs/), a compose-suite guard test/launchd-plist.test.js that enumerates every *.plist.template under watch/, renders with fixed placeholders and strict-parses (T1 common shape, T2 exact ProgramArguments/WorkingDirectory, T3 README sed recipe placeholder-set == template set, T4 parser throws), plus mirrored README sections in watch/README.md (same subsection headings as the watcher's + the three-legged port block, stated as fact — AS-96 is cancelled) and the 'Links to Lattice' paragraph in apps/chat/README.md. Nine mutants in §5 with exact predicted failing sets; needs_human handoff text in §7 with the host commands verbatim. Two facts contradict the description (§0/§8): 8799 is now held by pid 52536 ('lattice dashboard', no args), not 37867, and a SECOND dashboard runs on :8805 (pid 78002) — so the stop step keys on the port (lsof -iTCP:8799) not on a pid; and plutil/launchctl/pgrep/lsof are not in the tick allowlist, so AC-1's plutil half is a host observation and the node guard is the in-suite half. Tailscale-serve persistence: time-box expired, default 'yes' applied, §7 asks for 'tailscale serve status' quoted at bootstrap. Branch feat/AS-94-dashboard-launchd and worktree .worktrees/AS-94 created from master 2c4d6d1.

Implementation complete on feat/AS-94-dashboard-launchd (developer-lena).

BUILT (2 commits, both under apps/chat/, none touching .lattice/):
- c614821 'add the Lattice dashboard launchd template and the plist guard' — apps/chat/watch/com.american-software.lattice-dashboard.plist.template (§2, verbatim from the plan: explicit --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8799, RunAtLoad/KeepAlive <true/>, PATH-only env, logs at data/logs/lattice-dashboard.{out,err}.log) + apps/chat/test/launchd-plist.test.js (§3, T1-T4, ~330 lines).
- 6c20d1f 'document the supervised dashboard in both chat READMEs' — watch/README.md gains '## Lattice dashboard (AS-94)' with the six mirrored subsection headings + the three-legged port table, and two Files-table rows; apps/chat/README.md 'Links to Lattice' paragraph replaced with §4.2's text (AS-10 rationale intact, env-table row untouched).

TEST RECEIPT (AC-6). Counted compose run from $W:
  docker compose -f compose.yaml -p asc-as94-lena --profile tools run --rm --build test
  ' Image asc-as94-lena-test Building' / ' Image asc-as94-lena-test Built'
  cardinality: 297 tests examined -> 297 pass, 0 fail. All four AS-94 tests visible in the container run.
Master baseline NOT independently measured (a second from-scratch build did not fit the tick's wall clock) — the branch adds exactly 4 tests and no other test file changed, so the expected master number is 293; the reviewer should measure it. Image removed afterwards; $W clean, scratch worktree removed, no launchd job installed, the two host dashboards untouched.

MUTANTS (§5, all 9 runnable ones; scratch = detached worktree /tmp/AS-94-mutant at 6c20d1f, never $W). Each applied-assertion verified before the run. Grade: node --test on the scratch copy, NOT a compose run — the plan asks for compose per mutant and that did not fit the 30-min tick; the guard is a pure-fs node file with no container-only behaviour, and the compose run above proves it runs identically in the image. Predicted -> observed:
  M-AC1 (delete </array>; marker 1, </array> 1->0)        {T1,T2} -> {T1,T2}  MATCH
  M-AC2a (0.0.0.0; count 0->2)                            {T2}    -> {T2}     MATCH
  M-AC2b (port 8800; >8799< 1->0)                         {T2}    -> {T2}     MATCH
  M-AC2c (WorkingDirectory /apps/chat; 0->1)              {T1,T2} -> {T1,T2}  MATCH
  M-AC2d (ADVANCE_REPO_ROOT leak; 0->1)                   {T2}    -> {T2}     MATCH
  M-KEEPALIVE (<false/>; 0->1)                            {T1}    -> {T1}     MATCH
  M-LEFTOVER (__EXTRA__ arg; 0->1)                        {T1,T2,T3} -> same  MATCH
  M-RECIPE (dashboard sed key -> __LATTICE__; 0->1)       {T3}    -> {T3}     MATCH
  M-ENUM (git mv drops the com.american-software. prefix) {T1,T2,T3} -> same  MATCH
9 of 9 exact, no wider/narrower set. Free extra red observed en route: with commit c614821 alone (template+guard, README not yet written) T3 was red — 'expected exactly 1 install block for com.american-software.lattice-dashboard, found 0' — which is the missing-recipe falsifier the plan asked sedPlaceholdersFor to have.

NOT DONE / DEVIATIONS:
1. plutil -lint: skipped, host-only and not allowlisted (§8.2). AC-1's host half is deferred to the bootstrap record. The M-AC1 host-side plutil red is likewise deferred to whoever has a shell.
2. AC-3/AC-4 host observations: not attempted — a tick installs nothing (§7).
3. Master-baseline compose run: not measured, see above.
4. Added beyond the plan, one line: the parser THROWS on a duplicate <key> (the M6 probe in §9 asked for it; T4 covers it as its 8th malformed input). Everything else is as written.
5. compose file is apps/chat/compose.yaml with the test service behind '--profile tools' — plan §5's command was right.

§7 HANDOFF — the exact commands for the needs_human ask are in the plan file §7 verbatim (ls ~/Library/LaunchAgents/; tailscale serve status; A: lsof -nP -iTCP:8799 -sTCP:LISTEN + pgrep -fl 'lattice dashboard' + kill the :8799 owner only; B: REPO_ROOT/LATTICE_BIN/LABEL + mkdir -p + the three-expression sed + plutil -lint + launchctl bootstrap; C: launchctl print | grep state/pid/last exit, curl 200, kill, 200 again within 30s; D: lattice dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8799 must FAIL to bind; E: lattice restart then print). AC-9 check: the B block is byte-identical to watch/README.md 'Lattice dashboard > Install' modulo the # comments — I copied the README block from the plan, so a reviewer diffing them should find zero substantive differences.

Ready for review. Resume point if anything above needs redoing: nothing outstanding in implementation; the open items are the reviewer's compose re-run + master baseline, and the host handoff.

VERDICT: PASS (code half). Per plan §7 the task goes to needs_human, not done — AC-3/AC-4 are host observations. Reviewer: agent:qa-ruben, cold; the implementer's comment was read LAST, after every number below was recorded.

FINDINGS FIRST — 3 findings outside the criteria list (0 defects blocking, 1 defect minor/non-blocking, 2 convention):

F1 [defect, minor, non-blocking] T1's label/basename rule is computed leniently: `LABEL_PREFIX + basename.replace(LABEL_PREFIX, '')` strips the prefix and re-adds it, so a template named `lattice-dashboard.plist.template` with Label `com.american-software.lattice-dashboard` satisfies the assertion. Observed on M-ENUM: T1 went red on the hard-coded filename list (`expected exactly 2 ... found 2: ...advance-watcher..., lattice-dashboard.plist.template`), NOT on the Label rule the plan §5 predicted. Same red set, different mechanism; the enumeration assert covers the hole today, so not blocking. One-line fix for the next touch of this file: `const base = file.replace(/\.plist\.template$/, ''); assert.ok(base.startsWith(LABEL_PREFIX)); assert.equal(plist.Label, base)`. Not fixed inline: it would require a compose-grade re-run I did not have budget for and the guard's behaviour on the committed tree is unchanged by it.

F2 [convention, owner: plan author] AC-9 says the §7 handoff's sed/plutil/bootstrap lines are byte-identical to the README Install block. They are token-identical but not byte-identical: §7 wraps the sed over 3 lines, README over 5. Diffed by eye; every substitution expression, path and flag matches. Recorded, not a verdict input.

F3 [convention, owner: orchestrator/tick] Board commit daa8183's message carried the implementer's suite count and mutant tally ("297/297; 9/9 mutants red") into master's git log, which is in the reviewer's session snapshot before the diff is opened. That is the AS-36 anchoring leak through the board-commit plane. My numbers were measured independently (below) and happen to agree; the leak is invisible afterwards, which is the point. Proposed rule: board-state commit messages at the `review` transition describe what is on the branch, not the implementer's measured results.

M6 probes past the list (4): (a) M-ENUM mechanism above; (b) parser duplicate-key handling — T4 carries a `duplicate key` case and the reader throws `plist: duplicate <key>`; the positive-parse control in T4 shows "everything throws" is not what passes; (c) `git diff master...feat/AS-94-dashboard-launchd -- apps/chat/README.md` shows exactly one hunk, the §4.2 paragraph — env-table row and AS-93 prose byte-identical to master; (d) no file outside the four in the plan changed (Dockerfile, compose.yaml, deploy-shape.test.js, advance-watcher.mjs, watcher template all untouched). Not probed (time): T3 block-order swap; `|` in REPO_ROOT (README now names it in Prerequisites-adjacent prose, which is the plan's suggested handling).

SUITE (AC-6): `docker compose -f .worktrees/AS-94/apps/chat/compose.yaml -p asc-as94-ruben --profile tools run --rm --build test` — receipt line `Image asc-as94-ruben-test Built`; cardinality 297 tests, 297 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. The branch adds one test file with 4 `test()` calls (node-grade run of that file alone: 4/4), so master baseline is 293 by subtraction; I did not spend a second compose run measuring master directly.

MUTANTS (AC-7), node --test grade on a detached scratch worktree (.worktrees/AS-94-mutant, removed after), each asserted applied with `git diff --stat`/`status --porcelain` naming exactly the intended file, each restored with `git checkout -- .` (M-ENUM: `reset --hard`), task worktree proven clean with `git diff --exit-code`:
  M-AC1 (drop </array>) -> {T1,T2} = predicted
  M-AC2a (0.0.0.0) -> {T2} = predicted; failure message reads "bind stays 127.0.0.1 — tailnet reach is Tailscale serve only (CTO decision 1)"
  M-AC2b (8800) -> {T2} = predicted
  M-AC2c (cwd apps/chat) -> {T1,T2} = predicted
  M-AC2d (ADVANCE_REPO_ROOT env) -> {T2} = predicted
  M-KEEPALIVE (<false/>) -> {T1} = predicted
  M-LEFTOVER (__EXTRA__) -> {T1,T2,T3} = predicted
  M-RECIPE (__LATTICE__ in README) -> {T3} = predicted
  M-ENUM (rename) -> {T1,T2,T3} = predicted set, mechanism differs (F1)
  9/9 sets exactly as predicted. Mutants were NOT re-run compose-grade (sandbox denies env-prefixed/compound commands and the time budget was 22 min); the compose run above is the branch tip, not a mutant, so no stale-image hazard applies.

FLOOR CHECK (acceptance criteria sweep, second, labelled as such — 6 of 9 verifiable in a tick, all 6 pass; 3 deferred to the host):
  AC-1 in-suite half: T1+T3 green, M-AC1 red on exactly {T1,T2}. plutil half deferred to the bootstrap record (no plutil in a tick).
  AC-2: T2 green with the exact six-element array; M-AC2a red on {T2}; tree clean. All other §5 rows observed as listed.
  AC-3: deferred — host observations, needs_human.
  AC-4: README carries "ONE owner", "Do not run `lattice dashboard` beside it", pre-bootstrap stop step with `lsof -nP -iTCP:8799 -sTCP:LISTEN` and `pgrep -fl 'lattice dashboard'`. Bind-failure quote deferred to the host.
  AC-5: watch/README.md gains the section with the six mirrored headings in order (Prerequisites, Install (launchd), Uninstall / restart, After any change..., Troubleshooting, + three-legged block) plus two Files-table rows; chat README paragraph replaced with the AS-10 rationale intact. Install blocks side by side: dashboard adds LATTICE_BIN in place of NODE_BIN, the lsof/pgrep/kill pre-step, mkdir -p, plutil -lint, and a curl 200 check in place of the watcher's tail -f; PATH is `$(dirname "$LATTICE_BIN"):/usr/bin:/bin` vs the watcher's node+claude dirs. Every other line matches in shape.
  AC-6: pass, receipt quoted above.
  AC-7: pass, table above.
  AC-8: no asc-as94-* image left (removed), no /tmp/AS-94-* (a /tmp worktree was created and removed within this review; sandbox refused reads there, so the scratch copy moved to .worktrees/AS-94-mutant, also removed), `git worktree list` = master, AS-94, AS-95 (AS-95 is the parallel lane, not mine), no launchd job installed, dashboards untouched — `pgrep` quote appended to the Lattice comment if the sandbox allowed it.
  AC-9: token-identical, see F2.

Inline fixes on the branch: none. Level: no rework. Route: needs_human with the §7 handoff.

pgrep -fl 'lattice dashboard' at end of review (AC-8): 52536 lattice dashboard (no args); 78002 lattice dashboard --port 8805 — both untouched.

Need: a host shell (board or live session) to bootstrap the dashboard launchd job and quote four observations back on AS-94. Code + docs on feat/AS-94-dashboard-launchd, PR https://github.com/malls/american-software/pull/1, reviewed (PASS on the code half; guard green in the compose suite with a Built receipt). Nothing is installed yet; a tick cannot run launchctl. About 5 minutes. The verbatim plan section 7 command block (steps A-E: stop the :8799 owner found by port, pid 52536 at review time, leave 78002 on :8805 alone; render + plutil -lint + bootstrap per apps/chat/watch/README.md 'Lattice dashboard > Install'; the four AC-3 quotes; the AC-4 second-copy bind failure; the SIGHUP bonus line; plus one tailscale serve status line) is posted as the second comment on the PR and is the README Install block, because the sandbox refuses a Lattice comment carrying those commands. Reply on the task or the PR with the quotes; if the second copy does NOT fail to bind, say so and the README's AC-4 sentence comes back for a wording fix before merge. Merge waits on the quotes; the install is not the merge's precondition.

ORCHESTRATOR NOTE (live-session tick, 2026-09-10): state reconciliation after the board merged PR #1 on GitHub. This task's needs_human is CORRECT and still open -- do not close it. Ruben passed the code half and parked it for the host bootstrap; AC-3 and AC-4 require four quoted host observations (launchctl print shows running, GET :8799 returns 200, kill the pid and KeepAlive relaunches within 30s, and a manual 'lattice dashboard --port 8799' fails to bind), and none of those has been recorded yet. The board merging the PR closed the CODE half only.

THREE LOOSE ENDS a future tick will trip on, left deliberately rather than cleaned up unilaterally:
  1. The merge came in as f4af258 'AS-94: ... (#1)' -- a GitHub PR-button merge authored by malls, not the local --no-ff merge the Git Methodology specifies. Nothing is wrong with the result (the code is on master and the diff is Ruben's reviewed diff), but the tick-side close-out that normally rides with a merge did not happen.
  2. Consequently .worktrees/AS-94 and the branch feat/AS-94-dashboard-launchd BOTH still exist, and the branch is fully contained in master. Standard close-out would remove both. I did not, because this task is still open and I would rather the next tick or the board decide than have a worktree vanish under someone mid-bootstrap. Removing them is safe whenever someone wants to: the branch is in master's history.
  3. The chat export / deploy check that normally rides a merge tick did not run for this merge either. Deploy state should be verified before anyone quotes a container-derived number.

WHY I DID NOT RUN THE BOOTSTRAP MYSELF, despite plan section 7 naming 'a live session' as an acceptable actor: installing a launchd job writes persistent configuration into the board member's ~/Library/LaunchAgents and creates a standing background service on his machine. That is a system-configuration change requiring his explicit go-ahead, and an autonomous loop tick is not the right thing to make it. The commands are already written out in the handoff comment above and in apps/chat/watch/README.md; they need a human to run them and paste the four observations here.
